aman: quick note from trying to onboard a partner: our sampleapps are inconsistent about whether request_id shows up in spans vs logs when redaction is turned on. reproducible in node and java today.
lucy: can you share the minimal repro and the log excerpt?
aman: minimal node ordering that hits it: 
aman: ```js
// server.js
app.use(otel.instrumentation()) // adds span attrs lazily
app.use(authMiddleware)         // sets auth headers
app.use(retryLib)               // may mutate/replay headers on retry
app.use(wireRedact)             // scrubs headers for the wire/logs
```
aman: logs look like: 
aman: ```
DEBUG 2026-04-10T14:02:01Z request_id=rc-001 received payload
INFO  2026-04-10T14:02:02Z request_id=rc-001 processing step A
WARN  2026-04-10T14:02:02Z retry triggered attempt=2
INFO  2026-04-10T14:02:03Z request_id=<redacted> processing step B
ERROR 2026-04-10T14:02:04Z trace_id=tr-99 span_attrs.request_id=<redacted>
```
aman: interesting bit: DEBUG/INFO logs on the initial attempt show the raw id, but exporter payloads (spans) for retried segments end up redacted. seems like two separate systems reading the header at different times/places.
priya: i ran similar against java sampleapp. there the filter chain ordering varied by framework: sometimes the redaction filter runs before retry, sometimes after. different frameworks lead to different user-visible behaviour.
omar: two practical mitigations: (1) snapshot a stable span attribute right when otel sees the header (e.g., telemetry.redwood.request_id.first) and treat it as immutable; (2) move redaction strictly to the last-mile (socket/write) so it never mutates the context used by spans. both approaches need exporter-side guardrails.
lucy: snapshot is safer cross-language, but exporters must never leak original values. we should add an exporter processor that hashes or drops any attribute matching our sensitive key list unless an explicit allowlist is set. feature-flag the change for hosted customers.
aman: agree. also noticed a log-level interaction: our debug logs (dev builds) include request_id early for troubleshooting, but when redaction toggles on in prod they flip to <redacted> while debug traces in local runs still show raw id. doc confusion. we should clarify what redaction means for log levels in docs.
priya: action items i propose:
- add snapshot attribute in sampleapps (node/java/csharp) behind a feature flag + unit tests that simulate retry permutations
- add an exporter processor (dev-only default) that scrubs sensitive attributes in OTLP payloads and unit tests verifying no raw ids
- update devex docs with a small matrix: SDK x retry-lib behavior + recommended middleware/filter ordering + log-level guidance
omar: i'll prototype exporter scrubber (hash-on-export or redact depending on flag). lucy can you own the docs matrix?
lucy: happy to. will include a short FAQ: "why do my logs show id but my span doesn't?" and a diagram of timing (instrument -> retry -> redact -> export).
aman: opened a tiny repro branch: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/compare/retry-redact-lv1 (WIP)
telemetry-bot: New issue opened: DEVEX-5599 "sampleapps: request_id appears in logs but missing from spans on retries when redaction enabled" https://issuetracker.internal/DEVEX-5599
lucy: let's also add an e2e check: run sampleapp against a test OTLP collector with redaction on, trigger retry, assert collector sees no raw request ids but spans include the snapshot attribute (value hashed/redacted at export).
priya: small compatibility note: python's retry libs often return fresh header objects so python was less affected in our first pass. document that in the matrix.
omar: also add a test for streaming endpoints — mid-stream retries can create mixed results if partial spans flush early. snapshotting helps there too.
aman: i'll file the PR for node + link to issue. tagging @omar for exporter review and @lucy for docs. thanks all :thumbsup:
